CANONICAL_NAME.value: FFTPACK -- Paul Swarztrauber's Fortran FFT package (NCAR, 1985)

VERSION.value: netlib.org/fftpack as served 2026-09-12 (per-file; no tarball endpoint)

value.lineage: fftpack (netlib historical distribution): the authoritative Fortran source as served by netlib.org, the authors' own channel

value.built_to: compute forward/inverse real and complex FFTs and related sine/cosine transforms in Fortran 77, mixed-radix
value.pressure: the O(N^2) DFT cost, plus the many transform variants (real, complex, quarter-wave) each needing its own optimised radix passes
value.success_means: transforms invert to the input within round-off; the classic NCAR reference results

ANCESTRY.value: fftpack (netlib historical distribution): the authoritative Fortran source as served by netlib.org, the authors' own channel

cut.note: one mechanism family (mixed-radix passes) driven by a factorisation, wrapped by real / cosine / sine / quarter-wave pre- and post-processing; a Fortran-77 body whose control flow is arithmetic IFs and GO TOs

organs.mechanism: try divisors from NTRYH = (3, 4, 2, 5) then 7, 9, 11, ... (odd numbers after 5); each hit appends the factor and divides; if a 2 appears after other factors it is moved to the front (lines 105-107); the result IFAC = (N, NF, f1..fNF) drives every pass below; the doc says the transform 'is most efficient when n is a product of small primes'
assumptions: trial division; N with a large prime factor falls through to the general pass
organs.source_boundary: the factorisation loop 101-107 in cffti1 / rffti1

organs.mechanism: for each factor stage with stride L1 and IP-1 sub-blocks, tabulate (cos, sin)(FI * LD * 2pi/N) for the stage's IDO points; stored consecutively so each pass gets a pointer WA(IW) advanced by (IP-1)*IDOT per stage; computed once, reused for every transform of the same N

for each factor IP in IFAC: choose the specialised pass (4, 2, 3, 5) or the general one; call it with (source, destination) = (C, CH) or (CH, C) according to a toggle NA that flips after each pass (the general pass reports via NAC whether it flipped); advance L1 *= IP and the twiddle pointer; copy CH back to C at the end if the toggle ended on CH
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: no in-place bit-reversal: the alternating-buffer scheme is how FFTPACK avoids the permutation step

organs.human_name: PASSF2 / PASSF3 / PASSF4 / PASSF5 / PASSF (general), and RADF*/RADB* for real data
organs.mechanism: radix-2 as read: CH(i,k,1) = CC(i,1,k) + CC(i,2,k); the difference is multiplied by the twiddle (wa1) into CH(i,k,2); the array is reshaped between (IDO, IP, L1) and (IDO, L1, IP) by the argument declarations alone (the same memory, two DIMENSION statements); for IDO = 2 no twiddle multiply is needed (lines 4-10); radices 3, 4, 5 are the same shape with fixed rotation constants; the general PASSF handles any prime with an inner loop (NOT read)
assumptions: Fortran column-major aliasing of one array under two shapes
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the butterfly is the whole arithmetic; the reshaping-by-declaration is the transposition step other FFTs do explicitly

evidence.ref: vault:fftpack-netlib/upstream/passf2.f:1-24; passf3/4/5.f by name; radf2.f by name

organs.mechanism: ezfftf: copy R to scratch, RFFTF, then scale and split the packed result into azero, a[], b[] (2/N, sign flip on b); cost: fold the sequence with its reverse using the cos table (K, N+1-K pairs), RFFTF of length N-1, then an unfolding recurrence (X(I) = X(I-2) - X(I-1), lines 33-40); sint / cosq / sinq are analogous folds (skimmed by name only)
assumptions: the symmetry of the wanted transform lets a shorter real FFT do the work
organs.source_boundary: the wrapper files ezfft*, cost*, sint*, cosq*, sinq*

pressures.condition: the discrete Fourier transform is an N x N matrix product; N in the thousands must run on machines where N^2 flops and an N x N table are unaffordable
pressures.resource_or_constraint: flops and memory of the era; single precision
pressures.failure_condition: N^2 cost; or an N restricted to powers of two
pressures.world_punishes: direct evaluation; a transform that only accepts 2^k
pressures.world_rewards: factoring the index set and reusing sub-transforms (the same structure whatever the factors)
pressures.observable_consequence: runtime vs N and vs the factorisation of N (the doc's 'most efficient when n is a product of small primes')
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: restrict N to 2^k (the world must include awkward N)
pressures.cheat_control: a transform given a precomputed N x N matrix must match to single precision and cost N^2; if the world scores it equal, cost is not being charged
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: spectral analysis / PDE solvers (Swarztrauber's use)

pressures.condition: applications need several related transforms; each written from scratch multiplies the code and the error surface
pressures.failure_condition: divergent implementations of the same butterflies
pressures.world_rewards: symmetry-exploiting pre/post processing around one kernel
pressures.observable_consequence: the wrapper files call RFFTF/RFFTB and never a pass directly

unexplained: the general-radix passes passf.f / radfg.f (any prime) are unread; their inner structure may be a distinct mechanism (a DFT of prime length by direct sums)
sint / cosq / sinq folds are assumed analogous to cost from names and sizes only
single-precision accuracy vs N is not measured (Techne's run had no oracle)
residue.note: the small-radix path (factor, twiddle, driver, butterfly, real wrapper) is fully read
